P1_axis_calibration._what: Scale AND origin fitted together from detected tick marks (curation/lib/axis.calibrate). The tick POSITIONS are stroked segments in the PDF's vector layer and the tick VALUES are PDF text spans; neither is a pixel read.
P1_axis_calibration.seed_sensitivity_finding: A single tick displaced by +3 px on a FIVE-tick fit produces a residual of about 2.4 px, which is INSIDE axis.calibrate's 2.5 px tolerance -- least squares spreads the error over the other four points, and the middle point of five equally spaced has leverage 0.2, so the residual is about 0.8 x the displacement. The metric moves (0.0 -> 2.4) but the gate does not trip until roughly +3.2 px. Recorded because a tolerance that is quoted without its leverage is a tolerance nobody has measured; on these panels it does not matter, since the observed residuals are 0.0000-0.0001 px.
P1_axis_calibration.held_out_tick_note: Fig. 1p's 10^6 tick is ABSENT from the vector layer, so that panel is fitted on its three contiguous ticks and the 10^5 tick is held out and predicted. It is a round number the authors DREW and the fit never saw.

P2_heldout_tick._what: Fig. 1p's 10^5 tick, predicted by a fit that never saw it. Tolerance 0.02 decades.

P3_category_label_mapping._what: Fig. 1n's two significance brackets end on group centres. The legend names the comparisons, so this is a second, independent witness to which x position is which lipid -- the rotated text spans are the first.
P3_category_label_mapping.legend_vs_drawn: the legend prints two P values for this panel, P(LC-1 vs ALC-0315) and P(LC-1 vs LP-01), both < 1e-15; the two brackets DRAWN run ALC-0315 -> LC-1 and LC-1 -> LC-5, so the second bracket's right end is LC-5 and not LP-01. That mismatch is recorded in 08_contradictions.csv and does not affect the x -> name mapping, which both the rotated text spans and the bracket endpoints agree on.
P3_category_label_mapping.metric: max |bracket end - nearest group centre| in pt

seed.what: label list rotated by one position

P4_markers_vs_drawn_mean._what: Each group's five mice are drawn as 1.61 pt white circles. We EMIT the mean rule the figure draws, not an average of these -- jittered markers that coincide exactly collapse into one path, so a marker average is biased by whichever dots happen to be separable.
P4_markers_vs_drawn_mean.why_fewer: markers at identical coordinates are one path; this is why the drawn mean is used instead
P4_markers_vs_drawn_mean.metric: max |marker mean - drawn mean| in decades

P5_chain_lengths._what: Every long chain is measured with curation/lib/chains.raster_chain_length over a Douglas-Peucker sweep; a count that holds at only one tolerance is refused by stage01's _stable().

seed.what: revert the centreline to an unweighted binary row mean (what this file did first)
seed.metric: Ta3 vertex count across the eps sweep
seed.note: this is the historical failure, not a synthetic one: the first run of stage01 refused on exactly this, reporting Ta3 = 19 at eps = 1.0 px and 18 elsewhere.

P6_label_end_cost._what: A trace that begins or ends at a drawn 'CN' or 'O' label gains one Douglas-Peucker vertex that is not an atom. Tb1's hexyl is 6 carbons by Supplementary Table 5 (6-amino-1-hexanol, CAS 4048-33-3) and runs label to label, so it measures that cost instead of assuming it.
P6_label_end_cost.metric: vertices - carbons, over two label ends

second_witness.note: one carbon either way moves Tb2's implied pitch by about 0.9 px against the Ta chains' 14.8.

P7_si_printed_formulas._what: The SI prints a molecular formula and an MW for each of the ten lipids the paper carried forward. Each must be realised by a member of the enumerated library.
P7_si_printed_formulas.metric: number of the SI's 10 printed formulas realised (an EXISTENCE check -- see the sensitivity finding)

seed_A_block_inventory_sensitivity.what: each block perturbed by one carbon (or one oxygen) in turn; metric = how many of the SI's 10 printed formulas are still realised
seed_A_block_inventory_sensitivity.FINDING: This check is nearly BLIND. Nine of ten one-carbon mutations leave all ten printed formulas realised, because the library spans a wide range of CH2 counts and moving one block by a methylene merely reshuffles which member carries a given formula. Only the Tb1 mutation is caught (10 -> 8), and only because Tb1 is the sole block carrying extra oxygens, so it constrains the O-count combinations. The existence check is therefore NOT what pins the block inventory. What pins it is (a) Supplementary Table 5's four CAS numbers and molecular weights, re-derived in 01_blocks_qc.json to within 0.024, which moves by 14 per carbon and so is sharp; (b) the Douglas-Peucker chain traces with their bond-pitch cross-check; and (c) for LC-1 only, the point check below.

seed_B_connectivity_THIS_CHECK_IS_BLIND.conclusion: The formula is IDENTICAL and the check does not fire. Mass cannot see connectivity. This is recorded as a check that is necessary and NOT sufficient, and it is why reference_structures.csv (C10) exists: the InChIKey skeleton DOES move, and the anchor compares skeletons against the structure Fig. 1l draws.

seed_C_mass_visible.what: LC-1's tail Ta1 changed C14 -> C13

P8_printed_statistics._what: Statistics the paper prints, recomputed. Necessary, not sufficient: QL_2026 reproduced every printed hit rate on bars up to 28% too high.

seed.what: subtract 7.0 from the last pair's sum

fig1_radar_percentages._what: Fig. 1e,f,j,k print the motif composition of each hit set as integer percentages. Read as PDF text.
fig1_radar_percentages.note: these are marginals of a hit set whose membership is not published, so they can be checked for internal consistency but cannot be reproduced from data we hold. They are NOT emitted as values.

P9_enumeration.stereo_note: 384 - 96 = 288 members carry a new stereocentre at the linker-derived carbon (every linker but L1, formaldehyde). The Ugi is not stereoselective and the paper reports no resolution, so these are stored flat and say so on the row.

seed.what: if two blocks were accidentally identical the distinct count would fall below 384

P10_nmr_integrals_vs_formula._what: For each of the ten named lipids the SI prints both a molecular formula and a full 1H NMR integral list. They must agree. Both numbers are the authors'; this curation contributes neither.
P10_nmr_integrals_vs_formula.metric: number of the 10 whose integral sum equals the formula's H count
P10_nmr_integrals_vs_formula.FINDING: 9 of 10 agree exactly. LC-lipid-5's integrals sum to 107 against a printed C54H105 -- the paper is internally inconsistent by 2H on that one compound. Recorded in 08_contradictions.csv; it changes nothing we emit, because no SC/LC lipid is mapped onto a specific enumerated member except LC-1.

P11_oxygen_count_forces_the_subtail._what: O2 forces Tb2, O4 and O5 force Tb1. Cross-checked against the number of protons the SI reports in the 0.85-0.89 ppm terminal-methyl region.
P11_oxygen_count_forces_the_subtail.metric: number of named lipids whose 0.88 ppm integral is not 3x a methyl count available at that formula
P11_oxygen_count_forces_the_subtail.FINDING: All ten agree: for every named lipid, the protons the SI reports in the 0.85-0.89 ppm region are 3x a methyl count that is available at that formula. In particular SC-lipid-1 (C48H93N3O2) must carry the non-ester subtail Tb2, and the Tb2 members at that formula offer 2 or 3 terminal chain methyls, which covers the reported 9H.
P11_oxygen_count_forces_the_subtail.A_CHECK_THAT_WAS_WRONG_BEFORE_IT_WAS_RIG: The first version of this check counted methyls with a bare [CH3X4] SMARTS. That counts a pivaldehyde tert-butyl's three methyls, which resonate near 1.0 ppm and are NOT in the 0.88 ppm region, and it reported five of ten lipids as inconsistent -- including a confident paragraph about SC-lipid-1 that was simply an artefact of the wrong SMARTS. Recorded rather than quietly deleted: a check that fires is not thereby correct, and this one had to be made to agree with chemistry before its disagreement meant anything.

P12_anchor_independence._what: Whether the C10 anchor in reference_structures.csv was built by a route that shares anything with the enumerator. The test is on the GENERATOR'S fragments, not on the emitted string.
P12_anchor_independence.why_that_is_fine: both are canonical SMILES of the same molecule; a correct re-derivation MUST be byte-identical once canonicalised, which is exactly why C10's own anchor_may_be_a_copy missed F-037.
P12_anchor_independence.metric: longest common substring between any generator fragment and the enumeration's canonical SMILES, in characters
P12_anchor_independence.interpretation: The longest shared run is a plain alkyl chain ('C' repeated) plus an amide, which any correct representation of a C14 acyl group must contain. No fragment here is a slice of the enumeration: the decomposition, the strings' source, the machinery and the order all differ (see make_reference.py's docstring).

anchor_catches_what_mass_cannot.seed: LC-1's headgroup swapped H4 -> H3 in the ENUMERATOR only

_what: Stage 07 QC for SD_2026. Every check carries its number and a seeded defect that MOVES that number. One check (P7 seed B) is recorded as NOT firing, on purpose.

_deliberately_false: P7_si_printed_formulas.seed_B_connectivity_THIS_CHECK_IS_BLIND -- swapping LC-1's headgroup H4 -> H3 leaves the molecular formula identical, so the formula check cannot see it. The InChIKey skeleton DOES move, which is what the C10 anchor compares.
